text:
alex: Heads-up — seeing higher cold-starts for spot-backed inference pods in ap-southeast-1 this morning, especially on long sequences. Thinking warm-standby nodes + soft reservations to cut tail latency. Anyone on infra who can weigh in?

sam: How bad are we talking? p50/p95 cold-starts and eviction/retry rates?

alex: p50 cold start ~ 1800ms, p95 ~ 6.2s when a new node is spun and model KV has to repop. Eviction spikes -> ~3% request retry on heavy tails. Cost for 24/7 warm pool estimated +18% if we do full hot pool.

jess: I like warm standby but we should make it tiered: small warm pool for critical routes + predictive prelaunch for traffic spikes. Also set short cooldowns so we don't scale down instantly after a spike.

maria: +1 on tiering, but cost is the concern. Can we do soft reservations (reserve vCPU/GPU but don't keep model loaded) so the instance is ready faster and we lazy-load KV?

kai: We can adopt a mixed-capacity policy: keep N small on-demand or reserved instances (cheap set for critical qps), then let autoscaler use spot for bulk. When spot ramp rates are low, prelaunch extra spot nodes proactively. Use spot-price trends to decide prelaunch windows.

alex: Proposed experiment config (very rough):
```yaml
autoscaler:
  min_replicas: 4
  max_replicas: 200
  warm_standby:
    critical_routes: 2     # always-on small GPU nodes
    shared_pool: 0.3       # fraction of target capacity kept warm
  surge_ratio: 1.25       # allow 25% short-term overprovision
  scale_out_trigger: "qps_per_gpu > 1800"
  scale_out_cooldown_s: 30
  scale_in_cooldown_s: 180
  preempt_grace_s: 40
  fallback_policy: "on-demand-first-for_critical"
```

jess: Nice. A few suggested tweaks: make scale_out_cooldown 10s for aggressive ramp, but keep scale_in_cooldown >= 3m. Also add KV-prefetch hooks on node boot so model warmup overlaps with instance init.

maria: Can we measure cost delta quickly? I want to see simulated 7-day run with workload traces — tradeoff curve (latency vs cost). If warm_shared_pool = 0.2 vs 0.4, what are numbers?

kai: I can run a sim on Monday. Suggest we also add a soft metric for eviction-risk: if spot_revocation_rate > 0.8% over 10m, reduce shared_pool and increase on-demand fallback.

infra-bot: [alert] autoscaler/ap-southeast-1 spike detected at 2026-03-15T07:11:03Z — 18% increase in cold node creation rate.

alex: TL;DR decision request: run a 72h experiment with: warm_shared_pool=0.3, critical_routes=2 (on-demand), surge_ratio=1.25, scale_in_cooldown=180s, prelaunch window using spot price drop heuristic. If cost delta >12% or revocations >1.5% revert.
sam: +1 to experiment. Add canary on only two customer tenants first (prod-tenants a/b).
jess: I'll add the KV-prefetch hook (script + trace). Maria, tag you to review cost sim once Kai posts results.
maria: thanks — will monitor. If we see tail p99 > 10s, we abort.
kai: I'll schedule sim, implement spot-price prelaunch logic, and open the experiment runbook. Command to inspect candidate instance types: `gcloud compute instance-types list --filter="accelerator:gpu" --zones=asia-southeast1*`

alex: Action items: 1) Kai run sim + prelaunch prototype, 2) Jess add KV-prefetch + shorter outbound ramp, 3) Sam configure canary routing, 4) Maria own cost guardrail. I'll create ticket DEVOPS-3214 and schedule a 1-hr postmortem after 72h.

sam: one more ask — add a surge-shed route that will gracefully degrade non-critical features when on-demand fallback is used to save cost.

jess: noted — fallback can flip to low-precision/quantized model for non-critical requests. We'll implement a flag in routing policy.

alex: Great. Starting ticket and experiment now. Will post updates in this thread. Thanks all :rocket:
